text.p: British pharmaceutical group SmithKline Beecham Plc said on Tuesday that it had signed an agreement with Japan's Kissei Pharmaceutical Co to develop and market Kissei's cardiovascular drug Tranilast.
In a statement SmithKline said Tranilast is used to prevent recurrent narrowing of the coronary arteries which can occur following angioplasty.
Under the agreement SmithKline said it would have rights to market the drug world-wide with the exception of Japan, China, Taiwan, Korea and Russia. It will pay milestones and royalties on net sales.
The company said Tranilast is awaiting approval in Japan for its use as a cardiovascular drug.

The Japanese news agency, Jiji Press, said Tranilast, which has the brand name Rizaben, agency was first put on the market in 1982 to relieve nasal inflammation caused by allergies and skin inflammation.
Jiji said recent clinical tests have found that the drug is also effective in preventing the closing of arteries following angioplasty. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
